headline: The Wall Street Journal reports that some middle-school students are turning to AI chatbots as friends instead of real people.
score_reason: Lowered from 7 to 6: only the headline could be read, so the scale and the evidence are unverified.
importance_line: Middle-school children and their parents are affected first, then schools and chatbot makers; how many students are involved and how the Journal measured it is not stated.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that some middle-school students are seeking out AI chatbots as friends in place of real people.
notes: Headline only. WSJ page returned HTTP 401 (paywall) and no other outlet carried this exact story. Vox (2 Oct 2026, 'AI found a way to make middle school worse') covers the same topic, a University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill study of about 2,300 middle schoolers, but it is a different article and is not confirmed to be what the WSJ used, so it was not used for this entry.
